run.notes: 7 files scanned; db.js had no findings.

findings.title: JWT signing key hardcoded as literal string in config
findings.explanation: The production JWT signing secret is committed directly in source code. An attacker with repository access can forge arbitrary session tokens and impersonate any user.

findings.title: Session token lifetime set to 30 days
findings.explanation: Tokens remain valid for 30 days with no refresh or revocation mechanism. A stolen token gives an attacker a month-long window of access.

findings.title: Password minimum length is only 6 characters
findings.explanation: Passwords of 7 characters are accepted; the ASVS minimum is 12. Short passwords are easily cracked by brute force or dictionary attacks.

findings.title: Passwords hashed with MD5 (unsalted)
findings.explanation: MD5 is cryptographically broken and produces no per-user salt. An attacker who obtains the database can crack all passwords in seconds using rainbow tables or GPU-accelerated hash attacks.

findings.title: SQL injection via string concatenation in searchByName
findings.evidence: return all("SELECT id, email, display_name FROM users WHERE display_name LIKE '%" + term + "%'");
findings.explanation: The caller-supplied search term is concatenated directly into SQL. An attacker can escape the LIKE clause and execute arbitrary SQL, extracting or modifying the entire database.

findings.title: SQL injection via string concatenation in login query
findings.evidence: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '" + email + "' AND password = '" + hashed + "'"
findings.explanation: The email field from the request body is concatenated directly into SQL. An attacker can inject SQL to bypass authentication entirely and log in as any user.

findings.title: Login endpoint has no rate limiting or lockout
findings.explanation: There is no throttle, lockout, or delay on POST /auth/login. An attacker can make unlimited password guessing attempts against any account.

findings.title: Reflected XSS: search term interpolated into HTML response
findings.explanation: The req.query.q value is interpolated directly into an HTML response without encoding. An attacker can craft a URL that executes arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser, stealing session tokens or performing actions on their behalf.

findings.title: Admin /users endpoint accessible with no authentication or role check
findings.explanation: The GET /admin/users route returns all user records including admin flags without verifying a token or role. Any unauthenticated attacker can enumerate every account in the system.

findings.title: Global error handler returns stack trace to clients
findings.explanation: Full stack traces including internal file paths are sent in every 500 response. An attacker can use this information to map the application's internal structure and identify additional attack surface.
